top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock (Katori and Ye) is a mature, independently reproduced achievement: magic-wavelength trapping lets many atoms be interrogated free of first-order light shift and Doppler/recoil broadening, and RIKEN, JILA, NIST, PTB, SYRTE and NPL agree at the 1e-18 level in direct comparisons. It is distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-system prizes, and the two-name allocation has no arbitrary cut among the principals, provided the citation names the many-atom lattice. P002 is a strong science case but its credit structure (Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, 3D work, Mele versus Hasan) and overlap with the 2016 prize are unresolved, and no award is worse than a sound award available now.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no collaboration with Katori, Ye, Kane, Mele or Molenkamp, and my field is astroparticle physics and detector instrumentation
